correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the exact odd-prime LTE identity and proves the prime-power order formula. Chinese remaindering gives ord_n as the lcm; for each p its p-adic valuation is max(M_p, max(0,a_p-h_p)). A second LTE step yields v_p(b^L-1)=max(t_p,a_p), so the quotient valuation and both if-and-only-if conclusions hold for every odd n coprime to b. The assumptions p odd, p not dividing the base, finite support, n>1, and k>=1 are explicit. The package verifier independently tests 3422 direct cases and 549 support-exponent cases, but those finite checks are not a substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 1995 Franco–Pomerance full four-page article gives the definition and a sufficient obstruction; the 2026 Siegel full paper gives asymptotics, a squarefree sufficient criterion, a squarefree Wieferich-factor obstruction, and a nonsquarefree counting bound. Neither gives exact cross-prime exponent thresholds or a first-power formula. The OEIS A182297 listing and A237292 order-ratio identity represent actual exact membership data/alternative expressions but do not determine the full prime-support orthant. The result is a natural explicit characterization, with substantial residual risk of an uncatalogued derivation from known LTE.
residual_risks: Order lifting and CRT are classical; an explicit earlier criterion using the same ingredients could exist without prominent indexing.
The order-ratio database identity is an alternative full pointwise characterization; its combination with standard lifting makes priority sensitive to what counts as previously implicit.
No independent mathematical originality assessment has been performed.

value.rationale: The exact threshold provides a complete classification for every natural fixed prime support, including prime-power factors and cross-prime interactions, and gives the unique least support representative as well as exact first non-Wieferich power for every odd integer. Such qualitative all-support structural information is absent from the motivating asymptotic comparison and squarefree sufficient tests, and is useful for identifying/excluding arbitrary exponent patterns. Technical proof simplicity does not by itself make the natural complete classification a routine rephrasing. It is not claimed to settle global asymptotic distribution.
